cause: Pre-existing fork defect (backlog B53). GNU as 2.28 (GAP9 GCC) keeps R_RISCV_REL12=57 (lp.setup/lp.starti/lp.endi, 12-bit halfword field bits 31:20) and R_RISCV_RELU5=58 (lp.setupi, 5-bit field bits 19:15), PC-relative to the lp.* instruction. Upstream numbers them R_RISCV_32_PCREL / R_RISCV_IRELATIVE (67820e015fc7, 9f854c048997). int-20 ld.lld: 58 -> 'unknown relocation (58)'; 57 -> SILENTLY overwrites the whole lp.* instruction with a 32-bit PC offset (links, program wrong/hangs); fork numbers R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP/SETUPI=66/67 mapped to R_NONE by fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 (field left 0 silently).
fix: lld/ELF/Arch/RISCV.cpp only: helper pulpLoopFieldBits(type, loc) = 12/5 for 66/67, and for 57/58 only if the word at loc is an lp.* insn (opcode 0x7b, funct3 0/1/4 for 57, 5 for 58), precedent X86.cpp:102 R_386_GOT32X (llvmorg-20.1.8). getRelExpr: R_PC (replaces the fork's two R_NONE cases; checked in default: so 58 elsewhere still errors). relocate: unsigned range check (n+1 bits, error named R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP(I), negative shown signed) + 2-byte alignment + merge (val>>1) into the field, shape of R_RISCV_BRANCH (RISCV.cpp:390 @llvmorg-20.1.8); limits identical to fork RISCVAsmBackend (F010) and GNU as.

other_errors_seen: NEW, silent miscompile risk: LLVM MC resolves lp.setup/lp.setupi labels at assembly time even with +relax, so ld.lld relaxation inside the loop body moves the loop end but not the field. Repro logs/20-F027-evidence/t4.s: llvm-mc -mattr=+c,+xpulpv,+relax, 'call g' inside lp.setupi body relaxed to c.jal by ld.lld -> lp.setupi end offset 7 halfwords points 6 bytes past the real end. GNU as keeps R_RISCV_RELU5/REL12 so GNU ld/lld recompute it. Fix belongs in mc (emit R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP(I) when relaxation is on, like upstream forces branch relocations; lld now applies them). GAP9 flows use -mno-relax so not hit today.

Reverse interop: GNU ld 2.28 cannot link LLVM objects that carry R_PULPV2_LOOP_SETUP/SETUPI (66/67); if the mc fix above makes LLVM emit loop relocations under relax, GCC-ld compatibility would need GNU's 57/58 numbering (which clashes with upstream psABI) - owner decision.

GNU as 2.28 also defines R_RISCV_12_I=59 / R_RISCV_12_S=60 (fork RISCV.def moved them to 68/69); 59/60 clash with upstream R_RISCV_PLT32 / R_RISCV_SET_ULEB128. Not investigated which GCC constructs emit them; if a GCC object carries one, ld.lld would misapply it as PLT32/SET_ULEB128.
GNU objdump shows lp.* offsets >= 0x800 halfwords as negative (display only; hardware and GNU as treat the field as unsigned).
Pre-existing GNU as vs LLVM numeric-operand semantics difference (from F010) unchanged.
